items.snippet: To walk down Village Lane in Orient, known as Oysterponds prior to 1836, is to experience the East End’s past.

Shelter Island Heights Historical District was established as a summer resort in the 19th century, and still looks about the same. The quiet streets are lined with Victorian and Queen Anne-style summer cottages, and The Chequit still stands above Rainbow Park with sweeping views

Montauk Point Lighthouse is on the rocky point at the end of Long Island’s South Fork, surrounded by parkland and ocean.

The Oysterponds Historical Society is three historic buildings on 8.5 acres on Village Lane in Orient with exhibits of documents, furniture and implements of daily life in a 19th century summer resort.

items.place: The Coecles Harbor Marine Water Trail
items.snippet: The Coecles Harbor Marine Water Trail on Shelter Island follows the south shore of the harbor; a boat from Kayak Shelter Island is the best way to experience a place known for sailing, birdlife and scalloping.

The Coecles Harbor Marine Water Trail on Shelter Island follows the south shore of the harbor; a boat from Kayak Shelter Island is the best way to experience a place known for sailing, birdlife and scalloping.
Sculpture @ Sylvester Manor is an outdoor sculpture exhibit of East End artists on the grounds of a 300-year-old plantation and historic site.
Bug Light Cruises & Tours departs from Greenport every Saturday at 5 p.m. for a two-hour cruise to a lighthouse and back just before sundown.
Walking Dunes Trail takes you across shifting sands through rare native trees and shrubs, with views of Napeague Harbor from the crest of the dunes.
Little Creek Oyster Farm & Market offers a stellar selection of oysters on the half shell, from the East End’s best oyster farms, in a convivial bar and restaurant.
Greenport Harbor Brewing Company is one of the first and best of the East End craft breweries, with locations in Peconic and Greenport.
The Old Mill Inn is the restoration of an historic Mattituck speakeasy with a menu of local foods and a casual vibe.
Nookies offers a hearty breakfast at the Silver Sands Motel in Greenport with eggs, sausage and fluffy biscuits.
Stars is a cafe in the heart of Shelter Island, created by Pepe Martinez, a Mexican coffee roaster and his wife Lydia, a Slovakian baker.
Port is a lively waterside bar for boat and people-watching on the Greenport boardwalk.
Noah’s restaurant in Greenport is a lovely, fish-centric temple to the North Fork’s best seafood, produce and wine.
Estia’s Little Kitchen is a diner serving Mexican food just outside Sag Harbor for breakfast or lunch.
Clam Bar has been Napeague’s roadside seafood joint for over 40 years, and the place for a lobster roll or clams on the halfshell.

Wickhams Fruit Farm in Cutchogue (peaches, cherries, plums, pears, tomatoes) and Latham Farms (berries, melons, greens, garlic, squash) in Orient are standouts. Both farmstands are on land that the families have farmed for more than a century.

Orient Linen Company offers rustic and practical housewares and baby gifts in the village of Orient.
Wm. J. Mills & Co., in Greenport since 1880, made sails for oyster and whale ships, and in recent decades has added tote, travel and boating bags.
Preston’s Chandlery in Greenport is a historic marine supply store so close to the water it floods during storms.
Burton’s Bookstore has a small but mighty selection of contemporary books for children and adults.

The Shoals is a contemporary renovation of a classic motor inn with 20 rooms (and 20 boat slips) on the Peconic Bay between Southold and Greenport. It’s adjacent to a marina, and the Little Ram Island Oyster Company is next door. Summer room rates range from $359 to $995 a night.

The Menhaden is a boutique hotel with a private roofdeck bar in the heart of Greenport, an easy walk to restaurants, stores and the ferry to Shelter Island. It is a pet-friendly property with 16 rooms and summer season rates ranging from $449 to $999 a night.

Silver Sands Motel is a restored 1950s motor hotel with 33 rooms and bungalows on 1,400 feet of sandy beach on Pipe’s Cove at the end of Silvermere Road in Greenport. It has two restaurants, a diner called Nookies and Eddie’s for outdoor dining on the beach. Rooms start at $470 a

North Ferry A no-reservations car ferry between Greenport and the north side of Shelter Island runs daily from 5 a.m. to as late as 12:45 a.m. (check the schedule carefully if you are leaving after 11:30 p.m.) and takes 15 minutes to cross.
South Ferry A no-reservations car ferry between the south side of Shelter Island and North Haven on the South Fork, runs daily from 5:20 a.m. to 1:45 a.m. and takes less than 15 minutes to cross.
